Generate patient trajectories from imported cohort intervals

Source: R/trajectoryGeneration.R
createTrajectories.Rd

Apply the configured selection, transition and gap rules to a successful study import. See cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration for these rules and the required state definitions.

Usage

createTrajectories(
  cdm = NULL,
  studyEnv = NULL,
  trajectoryType = studyEnv$trajectoryType,
  runSavedStudy = studyEnv$runSavedStudy,
  oocFix = studyEnv$oocFix,
  outOfCohortAllowed = studyEnv$outOfCohortAllowed,
  cycleLength = studyEnv$cycleLength,
  stateCohortLabels = studyEnv$stateCohortLabels,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = studyEnv$stateCohortPriorityOrder,
  stateSelectionType = studyEnv$stateSelectionType,
  stateCohortAbsorbing = studyEnv$stateCohortAbsorbing,
  stateCohortMandatory = studyEnv$stateCohortMandatory,
  allowedStatesList = studyEnv$allowedStatesList,
  useCDM = studyEnv$useCDM,
  pathToStudy = studyEnv$pathToStudy,
  batchSize = studyEnv$batchSize,
  mergedStateOverrides = studyEnv$mergedStateOverrides,
  stopAfterAbsorbingEpisode = studyEnv$stopAfterAbsorbingEpisode
)

Arguments

cdm

A CDM reference created with CDMConnector, required when joining demographics with useCDM = TRUE.

studyEnv

Study environment returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration. Its settings supply the defaults.

trajectoryType

"Discrete" or "Continuous", ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. A choice is required for generation.

runSavedStudy

Whether to use restored saved-study settings. Import fresh data first. Saved runs do not accept analysis-setting overrides.

oocFix

Discrete gap rule: "None", "OUT OF COHORT", "Last present state" or a fallback state label. See cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration for transition and label rules.

outOfCohortAllowed

Whether retained state records may extend the trajectory beyond the target interval's end. The target start is unchanged.

cycleLength

Positive whole-number cycle length in days, within R's integer range. Required when generating discrete trajectories. It may be NULL during configuration. The final cycle is shortened at the observation boundary.

stateCohortLabels

Character vector of state labels. May be omitted when atlasStateCohorts is named. If both are supplied, the labels must match its names in order. Labels must be nonempty, non-missing and unique even when ignoring case. "0", "START", "EXIT" and "OUT OF COHORT" are reserved, including case variants. Labels may contain spaces or punctuation. They are separate from database cohort names and definition filenames.

stateCohortPriorityOrder

State labels from highest to lowest priority. All states within the observation bounds must be listed for discrete selection or continuous "Priority" selection. For a merged study, NULL uses a deterministic order of original states.

stateSelectionType

"First", "Overlap" or "Priority", ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. A choice is required for generation.

stateCohortAbsorbing

State labels that end follow-up when selected. NULL or character(0) means none. For an unmerged study, use exact configured or observed labels, or a named discrete fallback. Configured states may be absent from the current data. For merged studies, supply original state labels here and use mergedStateOverrides for exceptions.

stateCohortMandatory

Mandatory states used by the successful import. Rerun getDataForStudy to change them. Order and duplicates do not matter. NULL and character(0) both mean no requirements.

allowedStatesList

Named list of allowed destinations, for example list(A = c("B", "C")). Source names must be unique, nonempty and non-missing. Put all destinations for one source in a single entry. An empty list allows all transitions. character(0) or NULL in an individual entry permits no destinations. Nonmerged generation checks destinations against configured and observed states and any named discrete fallback, ignoring case. Unknown destinations are rejected before output files are written. Configured states may be unobserved.

useCDM

Whether to join age and gender from the supplied CDM. Otherwise, age and gender_concept_id contain NA.

pathToStudy

Directory containing the study folder. Generation uses the location stored in studyEnv.

batchSize

Maximum patients per generation batch. Supply one positive whole number within R's integer range. The default is 1000.

mergedStateOverrides

List of mergedState definitions. Requires mergeStates = TRUE. Supply at most one definition per membership set. Omitted properties retain inherited values.

stopAfterAbsorbingEpisode

Whether a selected absorbing state also excludes later episodes for that patient. The default, FALSE, lets later episodes start afresh. An absorbing state always ends its own episode.

Value

A data frame of class c2t_trajectories, also saved as a CSV in the study's Data directory. Printing shows counts and a short preview; use as.data.frame(result) for the ordinary data-frame display. See print.c2t_trajectories for printing options and the output vignette for the complete schema. The trajectory_definition attribute records the effective trajectory type, cycle length, ordered clinical labels and absorbing labels. TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis reads first-period definitions directly. All-period output uses version 2 metadata with episode identity and time origin, requiring an episode-aware downstream reader. Labels and absorbing status reflect merged-state overrides; configured but unobserved states remain declared. saveRDS() preserves this attribute; CSV output contains only rows and columns.

Boundaries and timing

Target intervals, labelled "0" in cleaned data, supply the start and end boundaries. The import's targetEpisodeHandling selects the first interval or all episodes. Patients without clinical state records remain eligible unless mandatory-state requirements exclude them. Discrete cycles include both endpoint dates, and the final cycle is shortened at the observation boundary. A selected absorbing state stops generation after its cycle. Its original onset date does not shorten that cycle.

Continuous trajectories end at the retained absorbing interval's end date. Earlier overlapping intervals are capped at that endpoint. START and EXIT are boundary markers and add no observed time. EXIT is on the day after the last cycle or continuous endpoint. Its time_in_cohort is elapsed years from trajectory start, using 365.25 days per year.

outOfCohortAllowed = TRUE can extend the endpoint using retained state records; it cannot recover records removed during import. A discrete state label represents the selected state for a cycle, without preserving exact event dates or ordering within that cycle.

Study workflow

Run getDataForStudy successfully before generation. A failed import blocks generation until a later import succeeds; previous patient files are preserved and are not reused for the failed attempt. The trajectory CSV is written after all patient batches finish, preserving a previous complete file if a batch fails. Unknown transition destinations are rejected before generation writes output files.

A completed fresh run saves Settings/analysisSettings.rds in version 6 format. Versions 4 and 5 also load with first-period behavior. See cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration for saving and sharing rules.

Labels and identifiers

State IDs are assigned once per study. In unmerged studies, START has ID 1, followed by configured states in their supplied order, additional input and discrete gap labels in alphabetical order, then EXIT. Configured states keep their IDs when absent from a batch. Merged studies use dictionary order and add state_key to the output. Their stateDictionary is available in studyEnv and Data/stateDictionary.rds. Use keys and membership for comparison between sites; state IDs are local to the study.

Patient identifiers are preserved. File and CDM input preserve large IDs and leading zeros as text. Canonical numeric IDs below 2^53 retain numeric output. Read subject_id as character when importing exported CSVs to preserve long or zero-prefixed identifiers.

See also

cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration, vignette("a03_trajectories", package = "Cohort2Trajectory"), vignette("a05_output", package = "Cohort2Trajectory")

Examples

cohorts <- data.frame(
  subject_id = rep("001", 3),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "Stable", "Complication"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + c(0, 0, 7),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date("2020-01-21")
)
folder <- tempfile("c2t-example-")
study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "example", pathToStudy = folder,
  useCDM = FALSE, trajectoryDataObject = cohorts,
  stateCohortLabels = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("Complication", "Stable"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority", cycleLength = 7
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
#> ℹ Importing data ...
#> ✔ Importing data ... [3ms]
#> 
#> ✔ Get cohort data success!
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...
#> ✔ Data cleaning completed!
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...

#> ℹ Saved cleaned data /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpUjaIV7/c2t-example-b47c4c341355/example/Data/importedDataCleaned.csv
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...

#> ✔ Cleaning data ... [25ms]
#> 
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)
#> ℹ Creating batch 1!!!
#> ℹ Saved trajectory dataframe: /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpUjaIV7/c2t-example-b47c4c341355/example/Data/patientDataDiscrete.csv
#> ℹ Saved settings to: /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpUjaIV7/c2t-example-b47c4c341355/example/Settings/analysisSettings.rds
#> ✔ Trajectories generated!
trajectories[c("subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date")]
#> <Cohort2Trajectory trajectories>
#> Patients: 1 | Clinical states present: 2 | Rows: 5 
#> Boundary rows (START/EXIT): 2 | Unresolved rows (OUT OF COHORT): 0 
#> Preview: 5 of 5 rows; 4 of 4 columns
#>   subject_id  state_label state_start_date state_end_date
#> 1        001        START       2020-01-01     2020-01-01
#> 2        001       Stable       2020-01-01     2020-01-07
#> 3        001 Complication       2020-01-08     2020-01-14
#> 4        001 Complication       2020-01-15     2020-01-21
#> 5        001         EXIT       2020-01-22     2020-01-22
#> Use as.data.frame(x) to inspect every column.
unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
